rationale:
structural: The text's structural obligations are the declared type and its trait implementations: `pub enum Label { Named(Vec<String>), Hash(String) }`, plus `Clone`, `Debug`, `PartialEq` and `Eq`. An alternative such as a struct with an optional name and an optional hash, or a `Named(String)` variant, could carry the same data but would break the prescribed variants and payload types. The trait list is also a clause. A hand-written type without those impls would break it.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/selector.rs#enum[Label]` is the only supplied root and is marked `{impl}`. It declares exactly `Named(Vec<String>)` and `Hash(String)`, and it has `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]`. That covers every structural clause.

The sentences about a named label carrying decoded parts and an anonymous label carrying the hexadecimal hash describe what each variant holds. The variant payload types express that. Which code builds these values, and how it decodes names or computes the hash, is observable behavior. It is not a structural obligation of this requirement, so I found no further root needed.

behavioral: The behavioral obligations are that a named label carries decoded name parts and an anonymous label carries the hexadecimal identity hash. The test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` covers both and asserts the outcomes.

- **Named label:** parsing `impl[Thing/Trait%3CT%3E]/...` asserts `segments[0].label == Label::Named(vec!["Thing", "Trait<T>"])`. This checks that the parts are split and that percent-encoding is decoded. The same test also builds `Label::Named(["a/b","c d"])` and asserts the encoded form `impl[a%2Fb/c%20d]`.
- **Anonymous label:** parsing `use@0123456789AB` asserts `segments[2].label == Label::Hash("0123456789ab")`. This confirms the hash is carried as a `Hash` variant, and it is lowercase hexadecimal.
- **Trait implementations:** `Debug`, `PartialEq` and `Eq` are used directly by the `assert_eq!` calls on `Label` values and on `Segment`, which contains a `Label`. `Clone` is used through `segments[2].clone()`, `clone()` on the segment, and `error.clone()`. These are structural, compile-time obligations, so no separate behavioral test is needed for them.
- **Enum shape:** The variants and field types are checked by construction in the tests. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the public export inventory, which is also marked as a test.

I found no behavioral obligation of the requirement that goes unchecked.
